The '''Cumberland County Jail''' is located in [[Portland, Maine]], and is the largest jail in the state. The jail, a division of the [[Cumberland County Sheriff's Office]], is a part of [[Cumberland County, Maine|Cumberland County]] government and is wholly operated by the elected Sheriff.<ref>Vergil L. Williams, ''Dictionary of American Penology''. Greenwood Publishing, 1996, p. 148. {{ISBN|0-313-26689-1}}.</ref> In 2002 it became the first jail in the state of Maine to receive national accreditation from the [[American Correctional Association]], at the time putting it among only 4% of adult correctional facilities in the US to have been so accredited.<ref>''Corrections Today'', June 1, 2002.</ref> It has the capacity to accommodate 600 inmates, and employs over 200 staff (including 130 Corrections Officers). Most inmates are serving short sentences or awaiting trial.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.wcsh6.com/news/article.aspx?storyid=70377|title=Cumberland County Sheriff Nixes Jail Consolidation|publisher=www.wcsh6.com|accessdate=2008-02-06|last=|first=}} {{Dead link|date=October 2010|bot=H3llBot}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://pressherald.mainetoday.com/story.php?id=141915&ac=PHnws|title=Lifting the spirits of souls behind bars |publisher=Portland Press Herald|accessdate=2008-02-07|last=|first=}} {{Dead link|date=October 2010|bot=H3llBot}}</ref><ref>{{cite web
